narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>The lowest common multiple of six and four is twelve, so they meet at the twelfth star.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Look at row one. Its twelfth star is grey, not blue.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twelve is the gap between meetings, because they first met at the fourth star.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble shows the twelfth star; the twelfth star of row one glows grey, not blue, while the twelfth star of row two is blue; the slip's bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>To find the next meeting, add the lowest common multiple to the first meeting place.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>To check, count along row one: the fourth, tenth and sixteenth stars are blue.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then count along row two: the fourth, eighth, twelfth and sixteenth stars are blue.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the words first meeting plus the lowest common multiple appear; the blue stars of both rows are counted: row one 4, 10, 16 and row two 4, 8, 12, 16 with ticks

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip says the lowest common multiple, twelve, is the place of the next meeting. Twelve is the gap between meetings, not the place, because they first met at the fourth star.
